acceptance: AGENTS.md 'Release pin' states the hazard and the remedy (after merging, restore next's version of each page main removed text from, unless the removal is a correction that also applies on develop)
The next-behind-main issue body lists docs files where the merge would delete lines from next, computed without writing a ref, with a test of the script against a scratch repository
No change to merge permissions, rulesets or the reminder's no-push design
Decision recorded: whether a checklist line in the issue is enough or the list of files is needed

Verification rubric: a scratch repository reproduces the 2026-11-14 case (a passage present on next and deleted on main by a later commit) and the issue body names that file; a case where main only adds text names no file

Until the guard ships, every main into next merge pull request description states that it was checked for deleted unreleased text (git diff origin/next <merge> -- docs blog shows no unintended deletions)
context:
Found 2026-11-14 while merging main into next after pull request #160. Guardrails: the workflow stays read-only on branches; do not auto-restore text; goes to main, then main is merged into next.

Review 2026-11-17: decision gate is the 'checklist line versus file list' choice, recorded by the owner before coding. The hazard recurs on every main into next merge, including the one after the v0.5.1 release pull request.

2026-11-19 owner decision: file list. The next-behind-main issue lists each docs/blog file where merging main would delete lines from next, computed in memory; a checklist line alone is not enough.

2026-11-19: implemented in PR #207 (scripts/next-deletions.mjs, sync-next issue list, AGENTS.md). Independent review: no blockers; fixes applied (conflicting files now listed for deletions outside their markers; tab-safe paths). Replay on the 2026-11-14 merge names exactly the 24 hand-restored files. CI blocked by an unrelated Explorer read-model 20 mismatch (core #4305); merge pending.
description:
Problem: when a correction on main removes text that describes unreleased behaviour, the following merge of main into next applies the same removal to next without a conflict, because next still held that text unchanged. The unreleased documentation then silently disappears from next and from the next release. On 2026-11-14 the merge after the docs audit had to restore 24 files on next by hand. AGENTS.md and the next-behind-main issue text only cover conflicts ('next keeps its text'); they do not mention clean merges that delete.

Outcome: the person merging main into next is told which docs files the merge would delete from or shrink on next, and AGENTS.md says what to do.
